newsitem.title: USA: Wildfire sweeps through exclusive Califoria area.
newsitem.headline: Wildfire sweeps through exclusive Califoria area.

text.p: Wind-whipped flames destroyed at least 12 expensive homes and damaged eight others in an exclusive Orange County community on Monday while firefighters battled a 750-acre (300-hectare) wildfire northwest of Los Angeles.
California's notorious Santa Ana winds, gusting up to 50 mph (80 kph), spread both blazes quickly and authorities ordered residents to be ready to evacuate if necessary.

Orange County officials said the blaze near the town of Tustin, about 30 miles (50 km) southeast of Los Angeles, appeared to have started in a tree near a home. The house burned and embers from the fire carried by the wind spread to other nearby homes.

Evacuation of the area, including two nearby schools, was ordered by the fire department as flames soared 500 feet (150 meters) into the air, but no injuries were reported. An evacuation center was set up in Tustin High School.
Three hours after the blaze started, Orange County deputy fire chief Chip Prather said firefighters were making "good progress" in containing the flames in a two-square-mile (five-square-km) area.

The Santa Ana winds caused havoc with power supplies in southern California Orange County, downing lines and leaving about 50,000 people without electricity at one point, said Southern California Edison spokesman Steve Conroy.

In Los Angeles County, a blaze quickly burned at least 750 acres (300 hectares) of brush near Calabasas to the northwest of Los Angeles in less than two hours and was still raging out of control on Monday afternoon.

Both fires were fought on the ground and from the air, but high winds were also hampering the efforts of water-dropping helicopters, turning the water into a fine spray that had little effect on the flames. So-called "super-scooper" planes which scoop up thousands of gallons of water at a time and then deposit them on the flames, were having more success.
No buildings were reported to be in immediate danger from the Calabasas fire but officials said they were alarmed at the rate it was spreading.

The Santa Ana winds, which spring up every October and often last for several weeks, were responsible for spreading the flames in the firestorms of October and November 1993, which destroyed hundreds of homes in Malibu, the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena and the Orange County city of Laguna Beach.

Firefighters said they were close to containing fully a wildfire that had threatened homes and businesses along a scenic stretch of California's coast in the Ventana wilderness area of the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty. It has consumed 668 acres (270 hectares).

Firefighters said cooler temperatures and a drop in the winds had given them the upper hand over the blaze, which broke out on Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco. The Big Sur fire was now 85 percent contained and firefighters said full containment was expected by Monday night.

About 750 firefighters were battling the Big Sur blaze on Monday, backed by four air tankers and eight helicopters. Officials estimated the cost to date of the multi-agency fire fighting effort at nearly $900,000 but said the total could reach $1.5 million.
The cause of the Big Sur fire was under investigation.
